title: Grandma's Market List
learning_objectives: Listen to a longer story and keep track of a list
Explain why the last item was hard to find and how the problem was solved
parent_prompts: Before reading: Grandma gives Lan a list of four things. Let's see if we can remember them all.
After page 3: What has Lan found so far? What is left?
After page 5: Nobody has limes. What could Lan do?
After reading: Was the fruit seller's idea a good swap? Why?

pages.text: Grandma gave Lan a list and a basket. "Four things," she said. "Eggs, a bunch of herbs, a fish, and three limes for the soup."
pages.illustration_brief: Grandma at a doorway handing a folded paper and a woven basket to Lan; morning light.
pages.audio_script: Grandma gave Lan a list and a basket. Four things, she said. Eggs, a bunch of herbs, a fish, and three limes for the soup.

vocabulary.definition: Words written one under another so you remember them.
vocabulary.example: Dad wrote a list before the shop.

pages.image_alt: Grandma at a doorway handing a folded paper and a woven basket to Lan.

pages.text: The market was loud and bright. Lan found the egg seller first. Six brown eggs went into the basket. One thing done.
pages.illustration_brief: A busy market lane with awnings; a seller handing Lan eggs in a paper cone.
pages.audio_script: The market was loud and bright. Lan found the egg seller first. Six brown eggs went into the basket. One thing done.
pages.image_alt: A busy market lane with awnings; a seller handing Lan eggs in a paper cone.

pages.text: Next, the herb stall. Lan sniffed. Mint, basil, and something like lemon. "That one," said Lan. Two things done.
pages.illustration_brief: Bundles of green herbs on a table; Lan leaning in to smell one.
pages.audio_script: Next, the herb stall. Lan sniffed. Mint, basil, and something like lemon. That one, said Lan. Two things done.

vocabulary.definition: A small open shop or table at a market.
vocabulary.example: The fruit stall had big yellow mangoes.

pages.image_alt: Bundles of green herbs on a table; Lan leaning in to smell one.

pages.text: The fish seller wrapped a silver fish in a leaf. It was cold and a little slippery. Three things done.
pages.illustration_brief: A fish on ice being wrapped in a banana leaf; Lan holding the basket open.
pages.audio_script: The fish seller wrapped a silver fish in a leaf. It was cold and a little slippery. Three things done.
pages.image_alt: A fish on ice being wrapped in a banana leaf; Lan holding the basket open.

pages.text: But there were no limes. Not at the first fruit stall. Not at the second. "The lime truck is late," a seller said. Lan looked at the list and frowned.
pages.illustration_brief: A fruit stall with oranges and mangoes but an empty crate; Lan looking at the paper list.
pages.audio_script: But there were no limes. Not at the first fruit stall. Not at the second. The lime truck is late, a seller said. Lan looked at the list and frowned.
pages.image_alt: A fruit stall with oranges and mangoes but an empty crate; Lan looking at the list.

pages.text: "What is the lime for?" asked the seller. "Sour soup," said Lan. The seller held up a small green fruit. "Tamarind is sour too. Try it."
pages.illustration_brief: The seller holding up a brown tamarind pod; Lan curious.
pages.audio_script: What is the lime for? asked the seller. Sour soup, said Lan. The seller held up a small green fruit. Tamarind is sour too. Try it.

vocabulary.definition: A sharp taste, like lemon or lime.
vocabulary.example: The green mango was so sour my face squeezed up.

pages.image_alt: The seller holding up a brown tamarind pod; Lan curious.

pages.text: Lan carried the basket home. Eggs, herbs, fish, and tamarind. Grandma read the list, then looked in the basket, then laughed. "Not on the list. But it will do."
pages.illustration_brief: Grandma peering into the basket, smiling; Lan a little nervous.
pages.audio_script: Lan carried the basket home. Eggs, herbs, fish, and tamarind. Grandma read the list, then looked in the basket, then laughed. Not on the list. But it will do.
pages.image_alt: Grandma peering into the basket, smiling; Lan a little nervous.

pages.text: The soup was hot and sour and good. "Next time," said Grandma, "you write the list."
pages.illustration_brief: A steaming pot of soup on the table; Grandma and Lan with bowls.
pages.audio_script: The soup was hot and sour and good. Next time, said Grandma, you write the list.
pages.image_alt: A steaming pot of soup on the table; Grandma and Lan with bowls.

quiz.prompt: What four things were on the list?
quiz.explanation: Page 1: Eggs, a bunch of herbs, a fish, and three limes.

quiz.prompt: Why were there no limes at the market?
quiz.explanation: Page 5: The lime truck is late, a seller said.

quiz.prompt: Why was tamarind a good swap for lime?

options.text: Both are sour, and the soup needed sour

quiz.explanation: Lan said the lime was for sour soup, and the seller said tamarind is sour too (page 6). The soup came out sour and good (page 8).

quiz.prompt: Which thing did Lan find second?
quiz.explanation: Eggs were first (page 2), then the herb stall (page 3).

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up about Lan's trip: what was easy to find, what was missing, and what Lan brought home instead.
quiz.rubric: not yet: names one item; with support: mentions no limes with prompting; independent: three items found, limes missing because the truck was late, tamarind instead because it is sour
quiz.explanation: A retell that includes the problem and the reasoning behind the swap shows listening comprehension beyond the list.

activities.prompt: Put Lan's market trip in order.

items.text: Lan gets the list and basket.
Eggs, herbs, and fish go in the basket.

prompts: Why did Grandma laugh at the end?
If you could not find something on a list, what would you do?
What did Grandma mean by 'next time you write the list'?

off_screen_prompt: Write or draw a list of three things for someone to find in your home. See if they find them all.
